messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Severity P1 — private-vpc: gpu-serving queue growth for customer 'VerticaHealth'. Autoscaler alerts: repeated scale-up failures. Paging Alice Nguyen and oncall-ml.
Alice Nguyen: Ack, I'm on it. Seeing alerts for one private cluster in eu-west-1. Queue size jumping, 503s reported from proxy.
Carmen Li: How bad is the customer impact? Any timeouts hitting 5xx at the gateway?
Mateo Ruiz: Customer reported elevated latencies 10m ago. From our telemetry: queue length ~2300 requests, 90th pct latency > 15s, error rate ~22%.
Alice Nguyen: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -l customer=verticahealth` output shows many pods Pending/CrashLoopBackOff.
Ben Park: Looking at cluster autoscaler logs: `scaleUp: skipping because nodeGroup vertica-gpu-ng reached max size (10)` then `failed to provision: ErrImagePull` for the gpu runtime image. Autoscaler tried but group locked.
Carmen Li: So two problems: node group cap + image pull problems. Which is causing most of the backlog?
Mateo Ruiz: Both. Several pending pods are unschedulable bc of GPU resource scarcity; others failing to start with `ErrImagePull: denied` and long image pull retries, which blocks warmup.
Alice Nguyen: Paste logs: ```Autoscaler: pod vertical-triton-123 unschedulable: 2/3 nodes have insufficient gpu
kubelet: E0206 12:11:01 kubelet.go: failed to start container: Error response from daemon: pull access denied for registry.internal/rr-gpu-runtime:stable, repository does not exist or may require 'docker login'```
Ben Park: That registry is the customer's private mirror; looks like their mirror had an outage or auth token expired. Image pull rate limit isn't typical here — this is a 403/401.
Carmen Li: Any quick mitigation we can do without touching customer infra? Can we route traffic to hosted fallback pool?
Alice Nguyen: We have a fallback route but it's gated by the customer's rollout policy. They enabled fallback to hosted for emergencies but need a toggle from their ops contact. I've DM'd their SRE.
Mateo Ruiz: Meanwhile we can make autoscaler less conservative: increase nodegroup max temporarily, or add a temporary cloud autoscaler override. But that requires cust consent for dedicated cluster config changes.
Ben Park: Cloud console shows the nodegroup is at max=10, desired=10, but cloud quotas allow +4 nodes if we request. I can request immediate quota increase via internal flow, but that takes time. Alternative: create a new nodegroup under the same VPC with different AMI that pulls images from our hosted registry. That would bypass the customer's mirror.
Alice Nguyen: Good idea. Steps?
Ben Park: 1) create nodegroup `vertica-temp-burst` with gpu nodes, attach to same cluster; 2) label nodes so autoscaler can target them for GPU jobs; 3) set taint to prefer customer pods; 4) patch deployment tolerations. I can spin up a node manually via `cloudctl` now.
ops-bot: Action started: nodegroup creation requested by Ben Park. Request ID r-0a9f23.
Ben Park: Bootstrapping completed on 3/4 nodes; pre-pull script ran. One node failed with `EBS: volume attach timeout`, retrying.
Mateo Ruiz: I'm seeing pending pods drop from 2300 -> 600 as pods get scheduled onto new nodes. Error rate falling to ~6%.
Carmen Li: Customer ops (DM) just replied: "We can approve fallback to hosted for up to 4 nodes for 2h. Please proceed." :thumbsup:
Alice Nguyen: Great. Route toggles applied, ingress traffic rebalanced. Monitoring shows 95% of backlog cleared in ~10m.
Ben Park: Node with EBS attach failing recovered after retry; all 4 nodes ready. Autoscaler override removed after stable.
Alice Nguyen: Remaining work: investigate root cause of registry auth failure. I asked customer to check their mirror tokens; they say they rotated registry credentials ~6 hours ago and forgot to update the cluster secret. We've requested the updated secret and will coordinate a rolling secret update.
Mateo Ruiz: Impact summary for handoff: P1, VerticaHealth private cluster in eu-west-1; total queued requests peaked ~2400; ~22% 5xx at peak, customers saw degraded serving for ~28 minutes. Temporary mitigation: provisioned 4 burst nodes pulling from hosted registry; autoscaler override + fallback route used.
Carmen Li: Any ongoing risk? If their mirror rotates tokens again we could see recurrence. Recommend: (1) add registry health checks/alerting, (2) allow fallback for emergency without manual approval, (3) update docs for token rotation.
Alice Nguyen: Agree. I'll own a follow-up: postmortem, timeline, and action items. Assigning to oncall-ml for next 36h for monitoring and customer comms.
oncall-ml: Taking the follow-up. Leaving a runbook note: add a check in our bootstrap to verify `imagePullSecret` age and validity, and add heartbeat to detect registry 401 spikes.
Ben Park: Post-incident: reverting temporary nodegroup in 60m after sanity checks. Will keep logs for root cause.
Alice Nguyen: Closing pager for now, monitoring for 1 hour. Thanks all. :coffee:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to P2 — backlog cleared and customer confirmed degraded but recovered. Postmortem assigned to oncall-ml.
